concepts.title: Kindergarten Addition and Subtraction Worksheets Within 5
concepts.intro: Lily has two toy apples and gets one more. Instead of starting with a rule about the plus sign, let her move the two apples and the new apple into one group. She touches each apple once and counts three. The written equation records that action: 2 + 1 = 3.

concepts.title: Kindergarten Addition and Subtraction Word Problems Within 5
concepts.intro: Leo hears, “You have three counters and get two more.” He points at the two new counters and answers two. He has counted the change but not the whole group. Put down three counters first, add two beside them, and invite him to count everything that is there now.

concepts.title: Count and Write Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Mia points to a row of six pictures. She says the number words in the right order but touches one picture twice. Her final answer is seven. Before asking her to memorize more number words, help her coordinate one spoken number with one object.

concepts.title: Compare Picture Groups Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Ben sees three counters spread across a wide row and six counters packed close together. He says the wide row has more. Instead of correcting him immediately, line the counters up in pairs so that each counter in one group has a partner in the other.

concepts.title: Count and Circle Worksheets for Kindergarten – Free Printable Activities
concepts.intro: Choose a small group from a larger collection. Children circle the requested number of pictures and explain how they know when to stop. Read the directions aloud and accept any selection with the correct count.

concepts.title: Number Word Matching Worksheets for Kindergarten – Free Printable
concepts.intro: Connect numerals to the number words one through nine. Each board has three pairs and space to draw connecting lines. Read the words aloud so early reading skills do not become a barrier to the math activity.

concepts.title: Ordering Numbers Worksheets for Kindergarten – Smallest to Largest
concepts.intro: Compare three number cards and write them from smallest to largest. Use objects or movable number cards to explain the order before recording it in the answer boxes.

concepts.title: Before and After Numbers Worksheets for Kindergarten – Free Printable
concepts.intro: Find the number one step before and one step after a given numeral. Use a number path, counters, or spoken counting before writing in the two answer boxes.

concepts.title: Missing Numbers on a Number Line Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Read the first label, count forward by one, and fill the missing number. Each short line has five evenly spaced marks and a large blank below one interior tick.

concepts.title: Ten Frame Worksheets: Making 10 for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Fill each empty box with one dot, then write how many more make 10. Each frame starts with 5–9 pictures and gives children room to draw.

concepts.title: Make 10 Missing Addend Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Find the missing part that makes a total of 10. Begin with a written equation, then use counters or the open drawing space to show why your number works.

concepts.title: Longer and Shorter Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Compare the lengths of two bars with their starting points lined up. Circle the longer bar and record its label, A or B.

concepts.title: Sort and Count Shapes Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Find one kind of shape in each collection. Circle every match, then write how many you found. An adult can read the shape names aloud.

concepts.title: 2D Shape Recognition Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Trace each flat shape and name it. Use its sides and corners, not its color or position. An adult may read the names and write a spoken answer.

concepts.title: Counting Sides Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Look at the boundary, not just the shape name. Trace each straight edge once and write how many straight sides the shape has.

concepts.title: Repeating Shape Patterns Worksheets for Kindergarten
concepts.intro: Circle the first group of three shapes. Keep repeating that group in the same order, then draw the next shape in the box.

concepts.title: Missing Part Number Bonds Worksheets Within 9
concepts.intro: Split each pictured whole into two parts. Circle the requested number of pictures and record the other part. Choose two nonempty parts first, or practice a part with zero pictures.

concepts.title: Ordinal Number Worksheets for Kindergarten — First to Eighth
concepts.intro: An ordinal number tells where an object is in a line. Start at the left edge and circle just the picture in the requested position.

concepts.title: Kindergarten Addition and Subtraction Word Problems Within 10
concepts.intro: Move from small-group stories within five to joining and taking away within ten. Read each story aloud and let the child use counters, fingers, or a drawing before recording an equation.
